text:
maria chen: Heads-up — after I bumped our app to redwood-sdk@11.0.0 we started seeing auth header failures and a few streaming connections that never resolve. Anyone seen pkg-lock / runtime fallback issues during 11.x rollouts?

aj patel: yep saw related flakiness on staging. Noticed a transitive dependency on `http2-streamer@^2` got upgraded. Pinning it helped. :thinking_face:

david kim: For auth failures, 11.x changed the client config shape (old: `new RedwoodClient({ apiKey })` -> new: `new RedwoodClient({ auth: { type: 'apikey', key } })`). If you don't migrate, token refresh calls are skipped.

maria chen: ahhh that explains the 401s. We used the old shape in a few nested modules. Any recommended quick migration snippet?

priya shah: Quick diff we used in one repo: ```js
// before
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
// after
const client = new RedwoodClient({ auth: { type: 'apikey', key: process.env.RW_API_KEY } })
```

aj patel: Also note retry defaults changed: backoff base went from 200ms to 500ms and max attempts from 3 -> 5. If you relied on quick short retries for streaming reconnects, you might see longer hang windows. You can override via `client.config.retries` for now.

maria chen: good to know. The streaming hangs were more mysterious — connections opened but client never emitted 'end'.

tom lee: streaming change: SDK now requires explicit `signal`/abort handling in user code to get guaranteed teardown. Example: ```js
const controller = new AbortController()
stream.on('data', chunk => { /* ... */ })
setTimeout(()=> controller.abort(), 30000)
client.stream({ ..., signal: controller.signal })
```
If older code relied on process exit to close connections, that doesn't always work in certain runtime pools.

maria chen: thanks — we do have some helper wrappers that didn't pass signal down. Will patch.

david kim: For package locks: run `npm ls http2-streamer` or `poetry show --tree` to find the transitive. One pattern that saved us: add an explicit dev dependency to pin the transitive version in package.json, e.g., "http2-streamer": "2.1.4" and then `npm install --package-lock-only` so CI treats it consistently.

priya shah: If you need a short-lived mitigation while patching code, set env `RW_SDK_LEGACY_FALLBACK=true` on staging — routes to the legacy runtime that keeps the old client shims. It's not for prod long-term but buys time.

maria chen: where is that flag documented? I couldn't find it.

deploy-bot: Note: RW_SDK_LEGACY_FALLBACK is an internal feature-flag. Enabling will increase request latency (fallback runtime) and is rate-limited. Use only on non-prod or for short maintenance windows.

aj patel: ops tip: if you flip the flag, drain existing worker processes to avoid mixed client shapes in-memory. CI pipeline: add `npx redwood-lock-check` step to fail if package-lock drift detected.

maria chen: great. Plan: 1) pin transitive http2-streamer, 2) grep for old client shape, 3) add signal propagate in streaming helpers, 4) smoke test on staging with RW_SDK_LEGACY_FALLBACK toggled before prod rollout.

david kim: sounds solid. If you want I can run a quick search across monorepo for `new RedwoodClient(` and open a small PR with the config shape changes.

maria chen: would appreciate that — thanks! :pray:
